title: Thresholds and Delegated Decision Playbook for Open Model Ingest
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a concise playbook and numerical thresholds for admitting new open weights into the model catalog, and clarifies the delegated decision process for low-risk entries. The goal is to reduce manual gating for routine, well-scoped community variants while keeping strong runtime compatibility guarantees and clear rollback semantics.

Why this work now:
- We are seeing rising volume of community submissions that are low-risk but still require manual PM/Research review, slowing time-to-availability.
- Ambiguity in pinning expectations causes runtime surprises when a community variant diverges from a pinned baseline.
- Engineering needs explicit signals and pass/fail thresholds to automate initial admission and runtime probes.

Goals (what success looks like):
1) A deterministic admission score with clear numeric thresholds that can be computed by the intake service.
2) A delegated decision flow where designated Onboarding Reviewers can auto-approve submissions that meet low-risk criteria within the UI/API.
3) Defined compatibility metadata tags and TTL flags that the runtime can consume to select fallback behaviors and model-variant compatibility shims.
4) Acceptance criteria that map to automated checks (sanity tests, perf probes, KV/seq length heuristics) so engineering can build admission pipelines.

Scope in this ticket:
- Define thresholds and their rationale (ingest confidence, runtime probe pass rate, eval passband).
- Describe delegated decision roles, audit trail fields, and TTL/ephemeral flags for trial variants.
- Specify required compatibility metadata fields (arch hint, tokenizer id, kv-cache-stability, suggested pin policy).
- Provide acceptance criteria the engineering team will implement.

Out of scope:
- Changes to the serving runtime kernel selection logic (will be follow-up ENG tickets).
- Long-term policy on enterprise-pinning contracts for Sponsored Models (handled by a separate legal/enterprise PRD).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Admission score defined and documented: ingest_confidence = weighted(sum of static checks, eval_behavior_score, runtime_probe_score) with example weights and a default threshold of >=0.78 for auto-approve.
2) Automated sanity suite: each new ingest must pass a 50-sequence functional sanity suite with >=95% token-level match to expected outputs for deterministic ops or consistent sampling distributions for non-deterministic models.
3) Runtime probe policy: a candidate model must complete 100 synthetic invocations across typical seq lengths within the catalog's 95th latency SLO and have <3% error rate. Models failing probe thresholds are marked "requires-manual".
4) Compatibility metadata: every entry must include tokenizer_id, architecture_family (e.g., gpt-2 style, llama-family), kv_cache_compatibility boolean, and suggested_pin (pin | soft-pin | unpinned).
5) Delegated decision: Onboarding Reviewers group can approve any candidate with ingest_confidence >=0.78; approvals must record reviewer_id, justification, and a 14-day ephemeral TTL tag if the model is unpinned.
6) Fallback behavior: if a previously auto-approved variant regresses (runtime_probe_score drops below 0.65 or customer-facing error spikes >5% in 24h), catalog automatically flips traffic to pinned fallback and opens a rollback ticket with assigned owner.
7) Auditability: every auto-approve action and delegated approval must emit an audit event with links to intake checks, probe logs, and the reviewer decision.
8) UI/UX: console shows a clear badge for "Auto-admitted" vs "Manual-gated" and surface the ingest_confidence score and key failed checks.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (beta, 2 weeks): Implement ingestion score calculation and admin UI for Onboarding Reviewers. Enable auto-approve for "community-experiments" namespace only.
Phase 2 (broader, 4 weeks): Extend probes to 3 seq-length bands, wire audit events to console retention, and enable TTL labeling on catalog entries. Open opt-in to selected partner projects.
Phase 3 (safety, 2 weeks): Add automated regression detection and automatic fallback wiring; require security review for any candidate that opts out of pinning.
metrics:
- Time-to-publication for low-risk submissions (target: reduce median from 72h to <6h)
- % of community variants auto-admitted (target: 40% within 8 weeks)
- Post-admission regressions triggering fallback (target: <1% per month)
- Audit event coverage for auto-approvals (target: 100%)
